root_cause.text: The `sev_es_sync_vmsa` function in the KVM SEV subsystem fails to check if a vCPU's state is already protected (`vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected`) before synchronizing its state to the VMSA, allowing write operations to already-encrypted guest-private memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a check for `vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected` at the beginning of `sev_es_sync_vmsa` to return `-EINVAL`, preventing a host panic caused by an RMP violation page fault (`#PF: error_code(0x80000003) - RMP violation`) when accessing guest-private memory on SNP-enabled hosts.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent VMSA synchronization when the guest state is already protected by introducing an early state check.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check at the beginning of the sev_es_sync_vmsa function to return -EINVAL if vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected is true.
intent_record.how: This prevents the synchronization of the Virtual Machine Save Area (VMSA) if the guest's state is already protected, avoiding invalid state operations.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent VMSA synchronization when the guest state is already protected by introducing an early state check.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by introducing an early state check to prevent VMSA synchronization when the guest state is already protected, which is the exact root cause described.

candidates.rationale: This is the first logical check in `sev_es_sync_vmsa` before VMSA synchronization. The check for `vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected` should have been performed before this point to prevent synchronization when the guest state is already protected.
This is one of the local variable declarations at the start of `sev_es_sync_vmsa`, where the missing check for `vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected` should have been placed early in the function.

vuln_statements.explanation: The function sev_es_sync_vmsa proceeds to synchronize the VMSA without checking if the guest state is already protected (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected). This check should have been performed before this logical check to prevent writing to already-encrypted guest-private memory.
